source.title: Scaling Laws for Task-Stratified Knowledge in Post-Training Quantized Large Language Models
source.authors: Chen-Xi Zhou; Pengfei Cao; Jianguo Li; Bo-Han Yu; Jin Ye; Jun Zhao; Kang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study fits power-law relationships to post-training quantized model performance and evaluates prediction on held-out and cross-architecture configurations, using downstream accuracy transformed into a loss-like metric rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The study reports PTQ scaling results for adjusted downstream benchmark accuracy, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. It does not report training-token or training-compute sweeps, or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Figures 2–3 also describe trends, but their plotted values are not individually tabulated.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of downstream benchmark accuracy, transformed to -ln(Acc_adj), against model size N for post-training-quantized Qwen3 (0.6B–14B) and Llama-3 (1B–8B) models. It then checks extrapolation to a held-out Qwen3-32B. This is a new setting (weight-only PTQ) with a result on downstream predictability with scale (V6). It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, training tokens or compute, compute-optimal allocation, or architecture shape. Its bit-width, group-size and calibration-size laws are quantization-specific factors that no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that a four-factor power law (model size, bit-width, group size, calibration-set size) fits task-stratified PTQ performance on 293 configurations across Qwen3 and Llama-3. Reasoning is precision-critical, application scale-responsive, and memorization calibration-sensitive. Optimizing fine-grained factors is essential at low bit-widths to prevent collapse.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses GPTQ post-training weight-only quantization and fits benchmark-accuracy scaling laws over model size, bit-width, calibration-set size, and group size. It does not reproduce pretraining cross-entropy or training-compute/token allocation measurements from the original scaling-law studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted sensitivities vary across knowledge task levels and Qwen3 versus Llama-3; calibration-set effects are stronger in the 3-bit region and differ by task; 2-bit outcomes vary sharply with model size and task; inclusion of group size and calibration-set size improves fit, with the reported contribution of calibration data varying by task.

fits_no_version.finding: Quantized-model downstream loss-like metric follows power laws in log2 bit-width, log2 calibration-set size and group size. Group size and calibration sensitivities intensify at 3-bit (Cb elasticity -0.032→-0.103, G 0.073→0.117) and at 2-bit for N≥4B (G ~0.60 KM, ~0.33 KA; Cb ≈ -0.58).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training-quantized LLM performance scales as a power law in quantization hyperparameters (bit-width, group size, calibration size), with sensitivities rising at lower precision.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study evaluates downstream benchmark accuracy transformed into a loss-like metric rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy. Two-bit configurations are excluded from the overall fit, and low-bit behavior includes collapse and poor fits. The Qwen3-32B validation consists of 6 configurations and reports aggregate MAEs; the Llama-3 validation uses 42 configurations. The paper notes that its results are limited to representative dense Transformer architectures under weight-only quantization.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for individual benchmark scores or each of the 293 configurations: the paper primarily reports aggregate task-level scaling fits and selected validation errors. Figure-only performance surfaces and trend plots in Figures 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7 were not transcribed as individual values.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy; no token or compute sweeps.
No pretraining-loss extrapolation. The downstream 14B→32B extrapolation is recorded under V6.
No depth or width comparisons at fixed N.
No other modality or training regime. PTQ is post-hoc compression, not training.
Predictability from pretraining loss is not tested. Scale range is only 0.6B–32B; the effect of N is measured on quantized models only.
No test of parameter counting, schedule, data or fitting-method dependence of pretraining-loss laws.

missing.what: At 2-bit, models stay near the random baseline and improve only slightly with N, deviating from higher-precision scaling trends. This bears on V6 and is only shown as a figure trend.
In-fit MAEs (Qwen3 general 0.0267, KM 0.0219, KA 0.0254, KR 0.0361; Llama-3 general 0.0171 to KR 0.0227). These are needed as baselines for the 32B validation rows.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked nearly every row to V5, V6 and V7. I restricted the links to V6, because PTQ is not a training regime or modality and the quantization-factor exponents are not what V7 describes. The N-scaling is across separately pretrained released checkpoints, which likely differ in training data, so the N exponent is not a controlled parameter sweep. Extrapolation spans only 14B→32B. Adjusted R² values reflect all four factors jointly, not N alone.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy measurement; no training-token or training-compute scaling test.
The held-out Qwen3-32B validation is for adjusted benchmark accuracy, not held-out pretraining loss; the largest fit model is Qwen3-14B, so this is not an orders-of-magnitude extrapolation.
No fixed-compute comparison or loss-minimising allocation between parameter count and training tokens.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests the power-law form for weight-only post-training quantization and downstream knowledge benchmarks, not image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Tests predictability of downstream benchmark accuracy with model scale in quantized settings; it does not test predictability from pretraining loss.

Shows variation by task capability, architecture, precision region, and included PTQ factors. It does not test parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, or compute-optimal allocation in the original pretraining setting.

rows.subject: Qwen3 family
rows.operation_detail: Fit four-factor power law to aggregated general adjusted benchmark accuracy, using model size, bit-width, calibration set size, and group size.

conditions.value: 3/4-bit effective compression zone; 8-bit configurations fixed at Cb=128, G=128; 2-bit excluded
−ln(Accadj), with Accadj based on aggregated knowledge-level performance

rows.measure: Fitted exponents (N −0.359; log2 B −1.067; log2 Cb −0.032; G +0.073); adjusted R² 0.9425 in log-transformed space and 0.9475 in original accuracy space.
rows.baseline: Two-factor N,B model: Adj. R² 0.9125 in original accuracy space.
rows.value: Four-factor model: Adj. R² 0.9475 in original accuracy space.
rows.uncertainty: Standard errors and 95% CIs are reported in Table 7; exponent CIs: α [−0.374, −0.344], β [−1.189, −0.944], γ [−0.073, +0.008], δ [+0.060, +0.087].
rows.note: Aggregate fit across configurations, not a separate result for each model checkpoint. The paper describes the fit as having strong predictive capability.
rows.check: V5 link dropped: PTQ is not a training regime or modality, and the measure is downstream accuracy, not loss. V7 link dropped: exponent differences here concern downstream accuracy under quantization, not the fit-dependence of pretraining-loss laws. The N exponent (-0.359) shows predictable gains with scale, but the adjusted R² mixes all four factors.

rows.subject: Qwen3 family — general performance
rows.operation_detail: Fit the general scaling relationship using only 3-bit data and compare factor sensitivities with the broader fit.
rows.measure: Calibration-data elasticity magnitude changes from |−0.032| to |−0.103|; group-size coefficient changes from 0.073 to 0.117.
rows.baseline: Broader fit: calibration exponent −0.032 and group-size exponent 0.073.
rows.value: 3-bit fit: calibration exponent −0.103 and group-size exponent 0.117.
rows.note: The authors interpret the changes as stronger sensitivity to fine-grained PTQ factors in the 3-bit region.
rows.check: Reports only calibration-set and group-size elasticities in the 3-bit fit. These are quantization factors, not scale; belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen3 models with N < 2B
rows.operation_detail: Assess 2-bit performance across task levels and model sizes.
rows.measure: Universal performance collapse across all tasks; scaling-law fits fail to converge, with Adj. R² < 0 reported.
rows.value: Performance collapse; fitting does not converge (Adj. R² < 0).
rows.note: The authors state that PTQ tuning is ineffective in this size/precision region.
rows.check: At 2-bit, models below 2B collapse to near random and fits fail (Adj. R² < 0), so downstream accuracy is not predictable in this region. V5 and V7 links dropped.

rows.subject: Qwen3 models with N ≥ 4B — L1 Knowledge Memorization
rows.operation_detail: Fit or assess the 2-bit performance surface for memorization as PTQ group size and calibration data vary.
rows.measure: The authors report recovery when fine-grained factors are optimized; group-size exponent rises to approximately 0.60 and calibration dependence intensifies (γ ≈ −0.58). Adj. R² ≈ 0.91.
rows.value: Recovered scaling behavior under optimized fine-grained settings; Adj. R² ≈ 0.91.
rows.note: The paper describes recovery as conditional on smaller group sizes and sufficient calibration data.
rows.check: Reports the G (~0.60) and Cb (~-0.58) sensitivities of a 2-bit surface for N≥4B. These are quantization factors, not scale.

rows.subject: Qwen3 models with N ≥ 4B — L2 Knowledge Application
rows.operation_detail: Fit or assess the 2-bit performance surface for application as PTQ group size and calibration data vary.
rows.measure: The authors report recovery when fine-grained factors are optimized; group-size exponent rises to approximately 0.33 and calibration dependence intensifies (γ ≈ −0.58). Adj. R² ≈ 0.87.
rows.value: Recovered scaling behavior under optimized fine-grained settings; Adj. R² ≈ 0.87.
rows.note: Recovery is reported as conditional on optimizing the fine-grained PTQ parameters.
rows.check: Same as Q-2BIT-KM: G and Cb sensitivities only.

rows.subject: Qwen3 models with N ≥ 4B — L3 Knowledge Reasoning
rows.operation_detail: Assess the 2-bit reasoning performance surface across PTQ configurations.
rows.measure: The authors report reasoning fails completely; the surface is flat and Adj. R² ≈ 0.22.
rows.value: Flat surface with poor fit (Adj. R² ≈ 0.22); reasoning failure regardless of configuration adjustments.
rows.note: The authors contrast this with the recovery of memorization and application in larger models.
rows.check: The 2-bit reasoning surface is flat with poor fit (Adj. R² ≈ 0.22) for N≥4B, so reasoning accuracy is not predictable there. Whether N is an axis of the Figure 6 surface is not stated; the link to V6 is tentative.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v4 dated 21 April 2026; 293 denotes evaluated configurations, including validation and generalization, rather than configurations all used in one fit. Table 1 reports 165 fitted configurations, Table 9 lists 245 Qwen3 Fit configurations including 2-bit, and Appendix A.4 separately reports six collapsed 3-bit configurations excluded from regression.

statements.correction: Section 4.3.2: 2-bit Qwen3 with N<2B collapses across tasks, adjusted R²<0; 2-bit reasoning with N≥4B fails, adjusted R²≈0.22. Table 6: KM validation MAE 0.0946; fit MAE 0.0219. Fixed-total-bits comparison: not reported.
statements.problem: The collapse, fit statistics and memorization MAEs are supported. The study does not report a fixed-total-bits comparison showing 4-bit models outperforming 16-bit models, or corresponding 2/3-bit allocation results.
